tool_input.description: Replace host culture lookup with explicit German number format and run Money/Receipt tests, including in invariant-globalization mode

tool_input.command: dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~MoneyTests|FullyQualifiedName~ReceiptTests" 2>&1 | tail -5; export DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1; export DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_PREDEFINED_CULTURES_ONLY=0; dotnet test --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~MoneyTests|FullyQualifiedName~ReceiptTests" 2>&1 | tail -5; git stash -q; dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~MoneyTests" 2>&1 | tail -12; git stash pop -q; git status --short
tool_input.description: Run Money and Receipt tests normally and in invariant-globalization mode, then confirm the old code fails in that mode
Run the same tests in invariant-globalization mode

result:
- **Cause:** `Money.Format` relied on the host's culture data for `de-DE`, and runner-05 doesn't supply it. The Xping history shows this test fails only on runner-05 (including on `main@32f21f2`) and passes on runners 01–04 and 06, so it is not caused by this MR. My guess is that runner-05 runs in globalization-invariant mode or lacks ICU; I couldn't inspect the runner to confirm.
- **Action:** Changed `src/Storefront/Invoices/Money.cs` (production code, not the test) to use an explicit `NumberFormatInfo` with `.` for thousands and `,` for decimals instead of `CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("de-DE")`. The output is now the same on every host.

The Money and Receipt tests pass locally (6/6). I couldn't run them in invariant mode to reproduce runner-05, because the command was blocked, so the fix is unproven for that runner until the pipeline runs.

The change is not committed or pushed, so the pipeline won't go green until you push it.

Runner-05 itself is still misconfigured relative to the others, and any other culture-dependent code would hit the same problem there.
